overview: White develops the knight and avoids the Nimzowitsch main lines with d4. Black usually answers 2...d6 (a Pirc or Philidor-like set-up after d4), 2...e5 (transposing to open games such as the Four Knights or Scotch) or 2...d5. The character depends on Black's choice; I could not pin down one main branch, so I treat it as a flexible, mostly quiet developing line.

white_ideas.idea: Develop naturally with d4, Nc3 and Be2 or Bb5
Take space in the centre while Black has a knight on c6 blocking the c-pawn
Transpose into an open game or a Pirc-type structure

black_ideas.idea: ...d6 and ...Nf6 or ...Bg4, a flexible Pirc-like set-up
...e5 transposing to a standard open game
Undermine the centre with ...d5 or ...e6 and ...d5

typical_structures.structure: Depends on Black's reply: Pirc/Philidor-like, or open game

character.notes: Not enough information; mostly quiet development unless Black chooses ...d5.

approach.notes: Offbeat; the Nimzowitsch is seldom chosen by strong players.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2...e5
sublines_that_differ.how: Transposes to the Open Game, e.g. Scotch or Four Knights with a different move order.

character.reason: Mixed set-ups; unsure of the main branch.

approach.reason: The Nimzowitsch Defence is seldom chosen by strong players.

plans.reason: No consistent plan across the branches.
